To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Generative models can be trained using non-adversarial techniques by leveraging pretrained classifiers for feature extraction.

1) by matching features of pretrained classifiers, GFMN achieves state-of-the-art performance for challenging datasets such as CIFAR and STL; 2) GFMN can achieve state-ofthe-art performance for ImageNet with a simple feature matching approach, which does not require adversarial training; and 3) GFMN achieves competitive performance on the challenging ImageNet dataset by using a simple matching approach, and can achieve state-of the-art performance with additional regularization techniques.

(1) we propose a new non-adversarial approach for training generative models, (2) we show that our approach is able to achieve state-of-the art results for challenging benchmarks, such as ImageNet, CIFAR10 and CIFAR100.

the following questions:
Can we use pretrained classifiers and autoencoders to train generative adversarial networks?
the development of a non-adverserial approach to generative models.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed method, GFMN, is the first method to achieve state-of-the art results on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 with just matching the first order statistics of features.
, for the datasets we have considered, GFMN can be a very effective alternative to adversarial training, and can even achieve state-of-the art performance.
GFMN is the state of the art in terms of image quality for unconditional GANs, while it is also competitive with state-of-the-art GANs in terms of Inception Score.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our method can achieve state-of-art results on CIFAR10, STL10 and ImageNet with just first order statistics, without the need of using adversarial loss.
we show how to train generative adversarial networks by matching features instead of matching the distribution.
our approach is able to achieve state-of-the art results for CIFAR10 and ST10, and comparable results to state-of-the-art approaches for ImageNet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by using the features from pretrained models, we can obtain state-of-the-art performance for generative models without using GANs.
, in order to train a generative model that can generate samples with high fidelity to the data distribution, it is not necessary to train a discriminator.
